new_plays_proposed.trigger: any winter (Nov-Mar) storage-lane read - EIA print expectation, weekly balance reasoning, or a day-lean that rests on a storage view
new_plays_proposed.read: gw_hdd (forecast, dated ahead) and the storage phase - against the knowledge that the res/comm heating term is UNSERVED (no HDD->Bcf/d converter exists; registry A-38)
new_plays_proposed.call: In winter the SIZE of the weekly storage move is set by res/comm heating, not power burn. Heating is the bigger mover on 33 of 52 actual months and on 10 of the 10 largest (STEO actuals, A-38), and on every November in the record power burn moves OPPOSITE to total demand. A burn-based size call in winter addresses the minority term: hold wide bands, reason heating-first from gw_hdd, and say plainly that the converter does not exist yet.
new_plays_proposed.mechanism: Isolated at the weekly horizon by four same-burn SAME-BREADTH pairs, each a November/early-December week against a January/February week, 219-369 Bcf apart with the power side held constant: the differing term is heating. 2021-02-25 -338 vs 2020-11-19 +31 (burns 168/174, both breadth 2); 2022-02-03 -268 vs 2022-11-10 +79 (197/197, br2); 2025-01-30 -321 vs 2024-12-05 -30 (248/256, br4); 2019-02-07 -237 vs 2020-11-27 -18 (171/172, br3).
requires: NOT SERVED: HDD->res/comm Bcf/d converter - registry A-38, the build this play's bands wait on
new_plays_proposed.scope: winter (Nov-Mar) storage lane only. Does NOT touch the summer lane (see weather.summer_burn_lane_exclusion - in summer the burn stack IS the model) or the HH lane (A-37). Blind-legal: every input named is non-price and never-masked or dated ahead.
new_plays_proposed.falsifier: If same-burn same-breadth November-vs-deep-winter week pairs stop differing by more than ~100 Bcf once weather-normal heating is accounted for - i.e. the gap turns out to be burn mismeasurement rather than the heating term - the size claim is wrong and A-38's converter build is mis-aimed. Also refuted if the A-38 weekly re-check on a full HDD join shows power burn matching heating's share of weekly variance in Dec-Feb.

dS -268 (burn 197.1, br2) vs 2022-11-10 +79 (burn 196.7, br2): 347 Bcf apart, same burn, same breadth, November vs February.
dS -321 (burn 248.4, br4) vs 2024-12-05 -30 (burn 255.8, br4): 291 Bcf apart at matched readings.
Every November in the STEO record: total demand +11.9 to +16.1 Bcf/d while power burn moves -0.46 to -1.87 - the burn stack points DOWN into the month total demand turns UP (A-38).

new_plays_proposed.trigger: winter day or week where wind/solar output is RISING while heating-grade cold is present or forecast
new_plays_proposed.read: grid_stack.bas.US48.wind_mwh and solar_mwh (served, period+2) against gw_hdd; on the weekly lane, the renewables delta against the storage expectation
new_plays_proposed.call: Renewables UP into cold is NOT bearish total gas - it is bearish POWER BURN and the draw comes through the heating meter anyway. DO expect a burn-based read to UNDER-call the draw on these weeks (the tank drains while burn reads soft). DO NOT read a wind surge as bearish the storage print in winter. On the daily lane the same structure eats a weather bump: a forecast demand rise lands on gas only net of the renewables move.
new_plays_proposed.mechanism: Wind displaces gas in the power stack while res/comm heating - invisible to EIA-930 - takes the draw. Measured: 12 of the 14 deepest breadth-0/1 winter weeks carry POSITIVE dVRE (renewables rising into the draw): -258/+1493k, -252/+1461k, -206/+680k, -200/+1608k, -197/+838k, -196/+3078k, -190/+1484k, -190/+1986k, -187/+2653k, -163/+3819k, -152/+3286k, -151/+110k. Daily instances: g22 20260629 (state served wind +660k MWh, gas -556k vs prior period; actual -1110 against a blind +325) and g20 20260601 (wind +1,071k - the largest wind move in the 60-day census - gas -1,271k, coal -529k; actual -990 against +350).
new_plays_proposed.scope: winter storage lane + any daily read converting a weather bump into a burn bump. Summer daily instances (0629, 0601) show the same mediation with cooling. Blind-legal: all inputs non-price, period+2, never masked.
new_plays_proposed.falsifier: Forward winter weeks with rising renewables AND heating-grade cold whose realized draws match the burn-implied size (no under-call) refute the masking claim. On the daily lane: forward days where a served renewables surge coexists with the weather-implied gas bump arriving in full refute the mediation form (0629/0601 class).

new_plays_proposed.trigger: forecast heating-grade cold arriving WITH falling renewables (an Arctic high is calm), with or without producing-basin freeze signals
new_plays_proposed.read: gw_hdd forecast + grid_stack wind/solar falling + freeze_risk basin fields (A-24f) + hydro state where available
new_plays_proposed.call: This is the correlated-failure tail (A-33): demand price-INSENSITIVE by obligation, the coal ramp spent or spending, wind gone, supply itself freezing. Burn and price DECOUPLE - measured burn can FALL on the most violent day because generators are curtailed to protect heating load - so every economic-regime model is OFF and the only questions are physical. Hydro is the buffer being DISPATCHED (it ran above its month p50 in three of the four sampled events); a DRY winter removes that buffer and is the unobserved worse tail.
new_plays_proposed.mechanism: The storage table's own tail members are this conjunction and nothing else at high breadth: the winter deep draws at breadth>=4 with falling renewables are exactly the named freeze events, while ordinary renewables-down weeks with no cold draw -9 to -81. The conjunction is what makes the tail: heating demand exploding AND the instant absorber absent AND (2021/2024) wellhead supply cut.
requires: NOT SERVED: hydro buffer state forward instruments (A-18/A-20)
new_plays_proposed.scope: winter tail regime only - a flag that switches the MODEL, not a magnitude play. When up, burn->storage->price reasoning runs backwards at the extreme (curtailment order) and A-31's ramp findings describe the transition INTO it, not behaviour inside it.
new_plays_proposed.falsifier: A forward cold+calm week delivering an ordinary draw with functioning price elasticity (no decoupling, no curtailment) refutes the flag's necessity at its stated strength. The hydro limb is separately falsifiable: a freeze event where hydro fails to rise above its month p50 WITHOUT drought conditions refutes the dispatch-buffer read - 2025-01-25..30 (593-642 vs p50 669) is the one recorded exception and rides with the play.

dS -241 at breadth 5, dVRE -2,748k - the Arctic-high week: the coldest week of the S113 confound set with renewables FALLING, because cold outbreaks are calm.
dS -173 at breadth 6, dVRE -1,791k - the 2019 polar vortex week.
dS -128 at breadth 6, dVRE -1,843k - the week into Uri's ramp.

The served aftermath: coal 3,103,423 MWh (the block-loaded plateau, period Jan-30) decaying 2.87M -> 2.39M -> 2.02M across g12 and 1.67M -> 1.57M into g13 - A-31's seventeen-day staged ramp-down, visible day by day in the committed states, with a +390k two-day re-ramp into the Feb-24/25 snap meeting a still-warm fleet (A-34's second-event case).

new_plays_proposed.trigger: deterministic seasonal structure - applies unconditionally to any winter stack read; not a conditional trigger
new_plays_proposed.read: national hydro output and its month-of-year position; reservoir/guide-curve state where obtainable (A-18/A-20)
new_plays_proposed.call: Hydro does NOT belong in the intermittent-renewables term. It is WINTER-STRONG - monthly p50 GWh/d: Jan 669-828, Feb 714-766, Mar 716-817 against a Sep-Oct trough of 501-565, in every year measured (2024, 2025, 2026; 2021 consistent on the pre-split definition) - and it was dispatched ABOVE its month p50 INTO the freeze events (Uri week 844-903 vs 766; Jan-2024 787-842 vs 689; Jan-2026 883/791/787 vs 828). Treat hydro as the reliability BUFFER being played: ~6.5 Bcf/d-equivalent at the January level, with the year-to-year January spread (669 vs 828) itself the tradeable variance. The failure mode is not a calm day but a DRY YEAR - the inverted-U's drought limb, UNOBSERVED in the sampled winters - and its forward instruments are slow and dated (reservoir state, guide curves, TVA planned releases), the information class that survives past the 5-7 day horizon.
new_plays_proposed.mechanism: Reservoir hydro is storage, not weather - operators hold it for winter reliability and spring melt refills it, which is why the cycle is high Dec-Jun and low Sep-Oct, and why event days show dispatch ABOVE seasonal norm rather than weather-driven loss. Pumped storage is excluded from the modern series by construction (EIA-930 split the WAT/PS columns), so the A-20 confounder is out of these numbers.
requires: national hydro daily (evidence series committed: data_records/us48_hydro_daily_S114.csv; live serving = grid_stack hydro, S113 rebuild, store on S3)
new_plays_proposed.scope: winter stack model and the Class-2 flag's buffer limb. Summer: hydro slides to its trough in fall, and the ~2 Bcf/d summer gas-fill shortfall is A-16's recorded number. Level alone cannot be signed at the tails (drought drawdown vs flood spill - the inverted U); this play carries the SEASONAL structure and the dispatch behaviour, not a level bar.
new_plays_proposed.falsifier: Refuted if a further year's cycle shows winter (Jan-Mar) p50 at or below late-summer (Jul-Aug) p50 absent drought; or if freeze events systematically show hydro FALLING below month p50 without drought (the 2025-01 exception becoming the rule); or if the drought winter, when it arrives, does NOT produce the outsized gas response the buffer framing implies.

instances.what_the_state_said: Uri week: 895/848/859/903/844 GWh/d against a February p50 of 766 - dispatched into the event (pre-split definition, hydro incl PS in 2021).
January 2024 freeze: 823/842/787 vs month p50 689.
The $30.72 window: 883/791/787 vs month p50 828 - at or above the strongest January in the sample.
THE RECORDED EXCEPTION: 593/623/642 vs p50 669 - slightly below, in the driest January of the sample. Rides with the play as its honest counterinstance.

new_plays_proposed.trigger: summer storage-lane read where a tail-size weekly build or draw expectation is being formed
new_plays_proposed.read: the breadth of gas-share rises across the served BAs for the storage week (from grid_stack per-BA gas_share, period+2, week complete before the Thursday print)
new_plays_proposed.call: The summer lane is the burn stack's home (res/comm at floor, A-38 scope) and the breadth count works there as a ONE-SIDED EXCLUSION, never a sorter: breadth<=1 nearly excludes a monster build (builds >=+100 Bcf: zero at breadth 0, one of 25 weeks at breadth<=1 - 2019-05-23's +100 - against 27 of 139 at breadth 2-6), and the only summer DRAW in seven years sits at breadth 0 (2024-08-15, -6, burn 316.8). USE it to gate tail-size calls and feed NO CALL (A-2); DO NOT rank mid-size weeks with it - the middle does not ladder (br2 shallower-loaded than br3, br5 deeper than br4).
new_plays_proposed.mechanism: In summer essentially all demand variance IS power burn, so a week where gas share rose almost nowhere is a week without the broad burn lift that big builds' absence requires. Possible mechanical contribution - share ceilings in consecutive peak weeks - is FLAGGED AS A GUESS and untested (D37: the story is not the finding).

new_plays_proposed.falsifier: A second summer week at breadth<=1 delivering a >=+100 Bcf build, or a summer draw arriving at breadth>=4, refutes the exclusion at its stated strength. The coverage falsifier: if adding the missing Southeast BAs (A-18) materially moves the breadth of past weeks, the count was a coverage artifact and must be re-measured before further use.

new_plays_proposed.trigger: before reading ANY weather_forecast.run_delta sign or magnitude into a lean, in any season
new_plays_proposed.read: d_gw_hdd and d_gw_cdd separately, the calendar month, and model_disagreement.summary as the authority channel
new_plays_proposed.call: A weather revision has NO season-stable sign or size mapping. (1) The HDD axis INVERTS in the cooling season: on the g18-g19 shoulder days the five biggest warm revisions (-1.00..-1.70 GWDD) delivered +420/+30/+370/+610/+1230 - five of five non-negative - while mid-size cold-adds (+1.31/+1.41/+1.56) delivered -1050/-530/-960. Removing cold in May is BULLISH (more cooling), adding it is BEARISH - the opposite of winter. (2) The SIZE axis inverts: the three largest CDD revisions of the census (+2.66/+2.51/+2.26) landed on the QUIETEST days (+230/-60/+180) while the violence sat at mid-size revisions. DO NOT scale an expected move by revision size. (3) The authority channel is model CONVERGENCE, not the revision: 0713 carried convergence 0.017 with every fresh instrument pointing down against a +550 posterior (D25's override day); 0511 carried disagreement 1.127 - the fourth-highest of the census - on the walk's worst day (-2190). High disagreement is a NO-CALL state (A-2), not a direction.
new_plays_proposed.mechanism: The revision is a DELTA on an instrument whose demand meaning flips with season (HDD drives heating load in winter and kills cooling load in the shoulder) - D28's transfer disease arriving on a delta instead of a level. The size inversion is consistent with broadly-seen multi-day revisions being already priced (the acceptance limb, A-24a) - CARRIED AS A STORY, not a finding.
new_plays_proposed.scope: every lane, every season - it is a PREREQUISITE map, not a signal. EIA print Thursdays are excluded from the sign claims (0528, 0604: the print owns the day and the weather panel is silent). Mediation days (0629, 0624) show the revision losing to the served generation stack - couple with weather.renewables_masking_flip.
new_plays_proposed.falsifier: Forward shoulder days where large warm-removals (<= -1.0 GWDD) deliver DOWN days at ordinary base rates refute the shoulder inversion. Forward days where the census's largest revisions deliver the largest moves refute the size inversion. If high-disagreement days (>=0.7 GWDD spread) stop containing disproportionate outcome width, the authority channel claim falls.

instances.what_the_state_said: The walk's worst day (actual +1740, blind -450, err -2190): HDD revision +1.02 in mid-May - which the inverted map reads BEARISH, aligned with the blind - under model disagreement 1.127, the census's fourth-highest. The honest state was NO CALL; the driver was positioning, not weather.
The largest warm revision of the census (-1.70) delivered +1230 - the shoulder inversion's largest member.

Convergence 0.017 (tightest in the census) with a -1.27 CDD removal, D-1 flow -1,225 SELL, and a served stack cooling off - every fresh instrument down; the posterior went +550 on a handed-down table (D25's B-0713). Actual -620.
Size inversion member: +2.66 CDD - the largest revision in the census - delivered +230, a quiet day.
Mid-size revision violence: -1.66 CDD on the print Thursday delivered -2050 (direction right across the board; magnitude 8x under).

new_plays_proposed.trigger: deterministic - the calendar month; applies unconditionally to storage-lane tail-size expectations in Oct/Nov/Mar/Apr, not a conditional trigger
new_plays_proposed.read: the calendar month, then the month's one-sided tail bound from seven years of listed weeks
new_plays_proposed.call: The storage lane's tails are ONE-SIDED BY MONTH, and the month where the sign is open has closed tails. Seven years, every week listed: OCTOBER builds only (+29..+129, zero draws in 32 weeks). NOVEMBER bounded both ways (-94..+107 in 29 weeks - no deep draw in seven Novembers; the model handoff month, where per A-38 power burn opposes total demand every year). DECEMBER-FEBRUARY is draw season with the monster tail (December alone: -213..-1, not one positive week in 31). MARCH one-sided DOWN (-200..+37 - winter-grade draws persist, build tail closed). APRIL one-sided UP (-37..+103 - draw tail gone). USE as month-gates on tail-size calls and NO-CALL inputs (A-2): an October or April deep-draw call, a March big-build call, or any November tail call sits outside seven years of listings and needs extraordinary evidence. DO NOT use as level forecasts - the market prices the seasonal level; our use is call-formation bands and the burn-stack validity window (the summer/burn model extends through NOVEMBER at the weekly horizon, not to the equinox).
new_plays_proposed.mechanism: Injection/withdrawal seasonality plus the A-38 handoff: res/comm heating sits at its floor through November (the burn stack still describes the balance) and lifts December-March (the heating term owns the tail). The shoulders also carry opposite hydro-buffer states measured S114: the fall shoulder sits at the hydro TROUGH (Sep-Oct p50 501-565 GWh/d - the year's weakest buffer would meet any early freeze; unobserved in sample, carried as structure not prediction) while the spring shoulder sits at the melt maximum (May 840-847) stacking with peak wind - consistent with G16's April injection-bleed block. Cross-ref D28: absolute HDD bars discriminate ONLY in shoulder blocks (g7 2/10, g8 4/10, g14 4/12, g15 3/12), so the shoulder is also where threshold conditions carry their information.
requires: cross-ref: weather.winter_heating_size_term (the Dec-Mar size term), weather.summer_burn_lane_exclusion (the burn lane these gates hand off to)
new_plays_proposed.scope: storage-lane weekly tail expectations in the four shoulder-boundary months. The g18/g19 census adds the shoulder's DAILY-lane facts: model disagreement is structurally elevated there (nine of the census's eighteen >=0.70-spread days are g18, late April-May) so the authority/NO-CALL gate fires more, and the shoulder HDD revision axis is INVERTED (see weather.revision_seasonal_sign_map). Blind-legal: the gate is the calendar.
new_plays_proposed.falsifier: Any October week drawing, any November week beyond roughly +/-120 Bcf, any March week building beyond ~+50, or any April week drawing beyond ~-50 refutes that month's gate at its stated strength - each is a single-week, listable event. The hydro-asymmetry limb is refuted if a fall-shoulder freeze arrives and hydro cover proves irrelevant to the gas response.

instances.what_the_state_said: November's build extreme: +107 - and November's draw extreme in seven years is only -94 (2019-11-21). The transition month's tails are closed both ways.
March's draw extreme: -200 at burn 172 - winter-grade, while March's build extreme across 34 weeks is +37. One-sided down.
For contrast with October: the file's only summer draw (-6) is an August week; October's 32 weeks contain zero draws, floor +29.
December: max -1 across 31 weeks - every December week in the record drew. The gate month before it (November) never draws deep; the month itself never builds.
